title: Soft Paws, Hard Truths: The Real Cost of Outdoor Cats
summary: A science-writing article from MITES Semester on what outdoor cats cost local wildlife, built from published research and two expert interviews.
question: How do you write about the harm pet cats do to wildlife for readers who love their cats?

sections.title: What I wrote
sections.text: For the MITES Semester science writing course, I wrote a short article for a general audience. It draws on published estimates of how many birds and mammals outdoor cats kill each year, and on interviews with ecologist Christopher Dickman and wildlife ecologist Tyus Williams.

sections.title: The approach
sections.text: The article argues that the debate over outdoor cats stalls on values more than on data. It starts from the affection owners have for their cats, then makes the case for keeping them contained with options like catios and leash training.

sections.title: Recognition
sections.text: The article was runner-up for Best of Science Writing at MITES.
